Move the `edgeTable` and `triangleTable` lookup tables out of the per-cell loop and into the overall class or global scope to avoid repeated reallocation [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence supports moving `edgeTable` and `triangleTable` out of the per-cell loop to avoid repeated reallocation. Additionally, the passage text confirms this by stating: 'Look at how many times you'd be reallocating the edgeTable and Tritable! Those immediately need to move out to the overall class.' All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
**Definition**: A variant of Marching Cubes that extends the look-up table to cases where the isosurface passes exactly through grid corners by perturbing the scalar field [S1].

The claim states that SnapMC is a variant of Marching Cubes that extends the look-up table to cases where the isosurface passes exactly through grid corners by perturbing the scalar field. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the passages: 'SnapMC... is a recently proposed algorithm that extends the original Marching Cubes look-up table to cases where the isosurface goes exactly through the corners of the background grid' and 'SnapMC perturbs the scalar field to avoid edge intersections close to grid corners.' The notes also corroborate these specific details.
supported
Natarajan (1994) was the first to consider interior "tunnel" ambiguities [S2].

The Portuguese text in Source [S2] explicitly states: 'Natarajan foi o primeiro a considerar a possibilidade da existência de “túneis” ... no interior do cubo' (Natarajan was the first to consider the possibility of the existence of 'tunnels' ... in the interior of the cube). This directly supports the claim that Natarajan (1994) was the first to consider interior 'tunnel' ambiguities.
supported
**Pitfall**: Excessive memory allocations inside the per-cell loop dominate CPU time, often more than algorithmic complexity [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that excessive memory allocations inside the per-cell loop dominate CPU time, often more than algorithmic complexity. Source [S3] explicitly contains the sentence: 'Excessive memory allocations inside the per-cell loop dominate CPU time, often more than algorithmic complexity.' Additionally, the passage confirms this by stating: 'In short it isn’t just the algorithmic complexity, memory allocations (and in the base this does a huge amount of them) take time also.'
supported
**Steps**: Cache previously computed field strength values at grid vertices to avoid redundant expensive field evaluations during the marching cubes pass [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that caching previously computed field strength values at grid vertices avoids redundant expensive field evaluations during the marching cubes pass. Source [S3] explicitly notes this strategy in the bullet points and confirms in the passages that 'Speeding up the underlying field evaluation (with heavy memoisation) seemed to mostly solve the performance problems,' where memoization is the technical term for caching. The evidence directly supports the claim.
supported
**Definition**: A method addressing interior ambiguities in Marching Cubes by comparing the scalar field value at critical points with vertex values [S2].

The claim states that the method addresses interior ambiguities in Marching Cubes by comparing scalar field values at critical points with vertex values. Source [S2] explicitly confirms this in the Portuguese text: 'o correto comportamento do interpolante trilinear é determinado através da comparação do valor do campo escalar sobre seus pontos críticos e sobre os vértices do cubo' (the correct behavior of the trilinear interpolant is determined through the comparison of the scalar field value on its critical points and on the vertices of the cube). It also mentions that Natarajan observed that the ambiguity problem can occur in the interior of the cube. Therefore, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
Eliminate the `gridCell` object abstraction and pass grid points/values directly to the polygonization routine to reduce object overhead [S3, unofficial].

The source [S3] explicitly states in the bullet points and the answer by Will Gore: 'I ditched the gridCell object as well, going directly from the points/values to the triangles' and 'Eliminate the gridCell object abstraction and pass grid points/values directly to the polygonization routine to reduce object overhead.' This matches the claim exactly.
supported
Perturb the scalar field values on the grid so that the surface is 'snapped' to the grid corners, avoiding edge intersections close to corners [S1].

The claim states that the method perturbs scalar field values on the grid to snap the surface to grid corners, thereby avoiding edge intersections close to corners. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in both the notes and the passages. The notes state: 'Perturb the scalar field values on the grid so that the surface is 'snapped' to the grid corners, avoiding edge intersections close to corners.' The passages reiterate: 'SnapMC perturbs the scalar field to avoid edge intersections close to grid corners. In particular, it changes the values on the grid so that the surface is “snapped” to the grid corners.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
Nielson and Hamann proposed the Asymptotic Decider to resolve face ambiguities [S4].

The evidence explicitly states that the asymptotic decider (AD) 'was developed by Nielson and Hamann' and that it is a method 'to solve the problem of “holes”' which arises from the 'face ambiguity problem' in Marching Cubes.
supported

The claim states that the 256 cases are reduced to 23 base cases using only rotational symmetry. The provided text explicitly states: 'In MC23, only rotational symmetry is exploited, which reduces the 256 cases to 23 base cases.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
supported
**Comparison**: Memoization directly addresses the bottleneck of field strength calculation, which profiling shows consumes significant CPU time alongside the MC routine itself [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that memoization addresses the bottleneck of field strength calculation, which profiling shows consumes significant CPU time alongside the MC routine. Source [S3] explicitly confirms this in the 'Notes' section (which summarizes the content of the source) and in the 'Passages' section where the author states: 'the bulk of CPU time is split between the marching cubes routine itself and the field strength calculation' and later 'Speeding up the underlying field evaluation (with heavy memoisation) seemed to mostly solve the performance problems.'

**Definition**: A variant of MC that uses 23 base topologies to produce a watertight isosurface without holes, solving the face ambiguity problem by only exploiting rotational symmetry [S4].

The claim states that the variant uses 23 base topologies, produces a watertight isosurface without holes, and solves the face ambiguity problem by only exploiting rotational symmetry. The evidence explicitly confirms all these points: it mentions 'Marching Cubes with 23 base topologies (MC23)', states that 'MC23 can produce a watertight isosurface without a “hole”', and clarifies that 'only rotational symmetry is exploited' to reduce the cases.
